text: ‍FT: Mexico's Claudia Sheinbaum puts faith in petrol price cap July 25, 2026 | 🟡 📰 The FT discovers Mexico's fuel price cap and files it under ideology: "a window into the ideology and modus operandi of Sheinbaum," part of "the populist vision." The authority quoted: business leaders "wary" of "interventionist policies." 🔍 Left out: the cap is a voluntary pact with retailers cushioned by fuel-tax relief the government absorbs — the "tightening supply" claim comes from unnamed executives. (Paywalled; analysis from indexed text.) • "a window into the ideology and modus operandi of Sheinbaum" • "Business leaders wary of president's interventionist policies" — subhead • "several executives say is already tightening supply and will be hard to sustain"

‍CNN: For years, the US went after Mexico's drug lords. Now it's looking at the politicians July 25, 2026 | 🟢 📰 CNN on Washington's pivot from capos to politicians — and for once the Mexican side gets the mic: Sheinbaum's sovereignty objections, analysts warning the move risks "poisoning the waters" of security cooperation, and a rare nod to US drug demand and gun flows. 🇲🇽 CNN notes the cartels "are also fortified by strong US demand for drugs and the illegal flow of American guns" — the context this genre usually omits. • "well-heeled politicians who allegedly accept dirty money to help the criminals" • "they risk poisoning the waters of bilateral security cooperation" — USC's Pamela Starr • "Is this a legitimate interest to fight organized crime?" — Sheinbaum

‍THE ATLANTIC: A Planeload of Informants July 24, 2026 | 🟢 📰 The Atlantic: leaked audio catches FBI intermediaries trying to recruit Baja California's governor as an informant. DEA chief Terry Cole says cartels and Mexico's government are "one in the same." Even a former US narcotics prosecutor: "I'm scratching my head on what the goal is here." 🔍 The same piece notes Mexico has extradited or transferred 100+ alleged criminals — while 269 Mexican extradition requests sit unapproved in Washington. • "They are one in the same" — DEA chief Terry Cole, on cartels and Mexico's government • "Once you uncork the bottle, there's no controlling what comes out" — ex-DEA acting administrator • "Are they saying they want to extradite me?" — Gov. 🎓🇲🇽 Cuautla gets 128 homes, 207 property titles — and 10 new high schools. "The housing goal for Morelos is now 24,000 new homes this six-year term." — Margarita González Saravia, Governor of Morelos Infonavit will build 13,000 of them with an 8.15-billion-peso investment. Sheinbaum also announced 10 new "Margarita Maza" public high school campuses for Cuautla, house-by-house social attention, and youth employment — the federal strategy to address the causes of insecurity after the mayor's arrest.

🏘️🇲🇽 514,000 new homes already approved — 43% of Infonavit's six-year goal. "Of the 1.2 million homes the institute has set as its goal, 440 housing developments are already approved — that's 514,000 new homes, a 43 percent advance on the six-year target." — Octavio Romero Oropeza, Infonavit director, in Cuautla Vivienda para el Bienestar aims to build 1.8 million homes for workers earning one to two minimum wages, deliver 1 million property titles, and restructure unpayable credits for 5 million families. Today in Cuautla: 128 new homes and 207 titles delivered.

🇲🇽✊ "Together, we will build peace and justice in this wonderful municipality." "We're going to build together, because this is everyone's work — families caring for their children, the state government, the federal government. And together, we will build peace and justice in this wonderful municipality." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, in Cuautla, Morelos Two months after Cuautla's mayor was arrested on organized-crime charges, Sheinbaum arrived with a federal reinforcement: house-by-house attention starting next week, 10 new public high schools, youth jobs through Jóvenes Construyendo el Futuro, and more National Guard presence. She pledged to return in three months to supervise.
